results.contract: The adapter implements append through get and put. This contract check identifies a missing concurrency guarantee; it does not claim to simulate concurrent remote writes.

optionReview.rationale: The adapter reads existing content and writes the combined result, so it does not promise atomic concurrent line appends.
Changing adapters does not give this generic read-and-rewrite helper an atomic line-append contract.
The adapter does not automatically acquire a shared application lock around the read and write.
Separators affect formatting, not concurrent read-modify-write interleavings.

results.contract: The S3 adapter creates a presigned PutObject request and returns its URL plus headers. No S3 SDK request or external bucket upload is executed.

optionReview.rationale: The generated request is for uploading an object, not downloading through GET.
Signed upload requests can require headers supplied separately in the returned result.
The signature describes an upload request; required signed headers must accompany that request.
The correct method alone is insufficient when the signature requires particular header values.

results.contract: The standard fallback link is inspected. Creating symlinks is intentionally disabled in the isolated fixture runner.

optionReview.rationale: This exposes the private disk rather than the intended public uploads.
This reverses the intended web-root link and target relationship.
That exposes a broader parent tree, including private files under the stated layout.
That maps the public URL subtree to the public disk’s root while leaving the private sibling outside it.

results.contract: RedisStore flush delegates to FLUSHDB. This is a documented/source contract; no shared Redis database is contacted or flushed.

optionReview.rationale: Whole-database flushing can remove distinct prefixed keys as well.
Connection naming is not a selective boundary for a flush of the underlying logical database.
A prefix helps namespace ordinary keys, but this whole-store operation uses flushdb.
Ordinary key operations use prefixes; the broad flush operation is the exceptional scope being tested.

results.contract: The pool result loop preserves request keys. Network concurrency is not benchmarked; the pinned Pool::as source also stores requests under the supplied alias.

optionReview.rationale: A named pool keeps the alias as the corresponding result key.
The result is a keyed response array, not a generated method-based service.
The alias identifies its own request, not another request’s successor.
Network completion order is not guaranteed, and an aliased result is addressed by its named key.

results.contract: Official Vite environment contract, default prefix and a referenced value. No Vite bundler execution is claimed.

optionReview.rationale: The VITE_ prefix opts a value into client exposure. A private source .env file does not make the resulting browser bundle secret.
Minification is not confidentiality protection for data delivered to the client.
Build-time substitution can expose the value without serving the original file.
Laravel’s configuration cache does not rewrite a built client artifact.

results.contract: Browser Fetch documentation contract with cookie and server-policy assumptions stated. PHP cannot execute a browser credential policy; no browser network exchange is claimed.

optionReview.rationale: That is the default restriction and still excludes this different-origin request.
Fetch defaults to same-origin credentials; include opts into eligible credentials for a different origin.
This does not grant credentialed readable access and produces an opaque response for this use.
That is a server response policy header, not the client credential-mode option.
